text_fidelity_a:
JOOLA Vision Pickleball Paddle with Textured Carbon Grip Surface Technology for Maximum Spin and Control with Added Power - Polypropylene Honeycomb Core Pickleball Racket Available in 14mm and 16mm My wife and I are pretty much beginner players, having only played in high school (a long while back) and coming into the sport anew. So please take that into consideration in this review.

I had the chance to get us each a new pickle ball paddle and I grabbed this JOOLA Vision Pickleball Paddle with Textured Carbon Grip for her. While these two paddles, both from JOOLA, are extremely similar in look, there are a couple slight variations. I think the main - perhaps only - thing we noticed in difference is that mine is slightly heavier. Otherwise, for these beginners, they are each excellent and very similar. Perhaps as we get better we will find other differences, but as beginners, we each love the paddle we have and to us, they are almost one and the same. Again, note that mine is blue and slightly heavier, while hers, this JOOLA Vision Pickleball Paddle with Textured Carbon Grip, is slightly lighter and black. But beyond that, they seem to us to be similar in build. Our hits are going to continue to improve along with our confidence. I have to say, I do notice the weight more, but I have no issue - and this ever-so-slight weight difference is one that does not affect my swing. However, my wife does say she prefers her lighter version.

The area we both love about the JOOLA is the grip. Without question, of all the paddles we have, the JOOLA's grip is the best, top of the heap, and the reason we'd (so far) pick a JOOLA over the others. As we get better, that may change. But for both of us, we feel far more connection to the paddle than we have with others. So in the end, grip alone sells us on this JOOLA Vision Pickleball Paddle with Textured Carbon Grip.
text_fidelity_b: JOOLA Vision Pickleball Paddle with Textured Carbon Grip Surface Technology for Maximum Spin and Control with Added Power - Polypropylene Honeycomb Core Pickleball Racket Available in 14mm and 16mm

text_fidelity_a: Athletic Running Sports Socks for Men Women 6 Pack MAUYA mx Premium Quality Cotton Cushioned Socks White Ankle Socks Mens Womens No Show Low Cut Sock Unisex Adult These socks made by MAUYA MX are awesome women's sports socks! I have to say though, I'm not sure about 42% cotton, 55% polyester, 2% spandex, and 1% nylon blended fibers. I tend to purchase socks that have a higher cotton percentage than any other fiber. Cotton is breathable and will wick moisture away from your skin as well as dry fairly quickly. So...55% polyester makes me kind of leery but at the same time realize that it will provide more strength to the sock. BUT....the comfort is out of this world. And the thickness of the sock should be durable for all the sports activities. These socks are reinforced at the heel and toes and have elastic at the top band. And they have divided them according to shoe size range which is fantastic as these socks fit me perfectly! Be sure to wash them first before wearing. All clothing manufacturers put "sizing" on their fabric which gives it a crisp smooth finish. You want to remove this coating especially if you have sensitive skin. I believe the mfg also wrote this on the band around the socks. Enjoy these comfy and extra cushion socks!

SABRE Runner Pepper Gel, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Reflective Hand Strap for Easy Carry & Quick Access, 35 Bursts, Secure & Easy to Use Safety, Optional Clip-On Alarm & LED Armband Combos I have always kept pepper spray in both my car and home for safety reasons, and even in my purse. There are times when the only thing you have to protect yourself may be just pepper spray. Whether it's an animal or person meaning to do you harm, having pepper spray may be the only thing that gives you that precious moment to get away and stay safe. Living in a Cleveland suburb, I have had close calls and pepper spray is a must for even our postmen, as you never know if those unleashed dogs are red zone or not.

The first time I found I needed any type of protection was when I was taking flowers to our family's cemetery in Cleveland. There were actually people in hoodies stalking us- I was not alone- to the point where my husband took his golf club out of the car and held it like a baseball bat. Just having the pepper spray attached to my arm is a huge relief. I don't have to get it out of the glove compartment or my purse- which I never carry when I'm walking or doing things anyway. For walkers or bike riders, this convenient arm band is a must for protection. If only the 3 teenagers abducted by Ariel Castro in Cleveland had pepper spray, what a different outcome that could have been.

Sabre Red made a Pepper Gel Spray in an earlier model of this armband type, which had a wider and unbelievably uncomfortable armband, and it never stayed on your arm. They redesigned the armband on this new model- it stays on your arm, it's very narrow (1 1/2 inches wide) and it doesn't hurt like the wide one. Just know that it is made of velcro- so it won't feel like a soft piece of cotton (the underside is comfortable enough though), but being narrow, I like that there is less velcro on your arm. I like the buckle on the band, to keep the end from sticking out also. You can make it as tight as you like and I have no slipping or discomfort at all. At 20 inches long, this band will fit all arm sizes- even those larger biceps.

The canister of the red pepper gel spray has an ON/OFF position for your safety. The tight elastic sleeve has the velcro strip all the way down the side of the canister, so you can attach it to the arm band anywhere. There is also a strip of reflective tape on the side for additional safety from vehicles if you are walking or bike riding at night. My sister is a bike rider and she had to use this pepper gel on an attacking dog. She sprayed the dog in the eyes and it kept running along side her bike trying to grab her leg. She said she sprayed it again hitting it in the nose and mouth- that slowed it down and the dog finally turned around. So, I guess with a dog, that sense of smell just keeps on going until it gets sprayed in the nose.

As for the gel spray itself, it goes the full 12 feet when sprayed. You will get some fine mist coming back at you when the wind is against you, so protect your face. Make sure you test the spray first, so you know how far the spray will reach and to make certain you have a good canister. Sabre Gel has made great improvements on both the armband and gel spray on this Pepper Gel Duathlete Arm Band. The arm band is nice and narrow, comfortable and stays put. The Pepper Gel has just a little mist spray back, so you still need to protect your own face. It's a great 5 Star Improved Pepper Gel Spray and Armband, that hopefully you will not have to use, but if you need to use it, it can truly be a life saver.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Runner Pepper Gel, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Reflective Hand Strap for Easy Carry & Quick Access, 35 Bursts, Secure & Easy to Use Safety, Optional Clip-On Alarm & LED Armband Combos

Outdoor Edge Brush Demon - Tactical Survival Outdoor Knife with 13.5" Carbon Spring-Steel Blade and Rubberized Non-Slip TPR Handle This knife was designed for Outdoor Edge by Jerry Hossom, a highly respected big knife expert who makes some awesome custom knives for big bucks. (Search the internet for "American Kopis" and you will see what I mean) His biggest emphasis is on self-defense and martial arts.

This particular knife is really cool looking and immediately inspires confidence when holding it in your hand. To check out how it functions I compared it to one of my Esee Lite machetes, a big knife that I have used for hundreds of hours after trying out several other large knives/machetes/hatchets/saws trimming trees and cutting brush. The Esee can be found for between $60.00-$70.00 and the Brush Demon is available from $50.00- $70.00, close enough for comparison purposes. The Esee is made in South America and has a lifetime guarantee. The Brush Demon also has a lifetime guarantee and is made in China.

The Esee has micarta handles, a blade length of 17.25", an overall length of 23.5", a blade thickness of .065", and weighs about 17 oz. The Brush Demon has a rubberized handle, a blade length of 13.5", an overall length of 20.08", a blade thickness of .160", and weighs about 18 oz. Both blades use a medium grade carbon steel that is black powder coated. These carbon blades are tougher, durable, easy to sharpen, but also susceptible to corrosion.

Blades are a bit like cars: some people like one design, some like another, some owners drive their cars gently, and some drive them to the edge of abuse. So when I give you a perspective on a knife, it's simply my perspective based on how I use it. My height, my weight, the length of my arms, how strong I am (or not), and the type of swing I use all come into play. So here is what I found after using both knives to limb trees and to chop into trunks. Most people would probably use hatchets or saws for this type of work but I have found that a big knife is more effective and can be used for a longer time without arm fatigue.

For me, the Esee Lite is the hands down winner. It is about 3.0" longer, resulting in better weight transfer with a full swing. The blade itself is about 4.0" longer and is markedly thinner and sharper. Having a blade that is less than half as thick as the blade on the Brush Demon results in more energy being driven deeper into the wood. If you compare the cut made with the wide blade of a hatchet to that of a good machete, the thinner blade of the machete will always cut farther into the wood with less effort. The same holds true when comparing the thickness of these two big knife blades. I also noticed that the blade configuration of the Brush Demon resulted in a much smaller "sweet spot" when cutting wood. The best cuts were made when the wood was impacted at the belly of the blade. Off-center hits were noticeably ineffective. The Esse Lite was better balanced and similar to hitting a golf ball with an over-sized driver--even a relatively poor impact had good results.

So with apologies to Jerry Hossom--and still lusting after an American Kopis--the Brush Demon doesn't stand up to the Esee Lite machete for the type of work I use it for. On the other hand, the pointed Brush Demon would probably do much better against soft targets--especially for stabbing. If I could only carry one survival knife with me, it would still be the Esee.
text_fidelity_b: Outdoor Edge Brush Demon - Tactical Survival Outdoor Knife with 13.5" Carbon Spring-Steel Blade and Rubberized Non-Slip TPR Handle

text_fidelity_a:
Bushnell Engage Riflescope Growing up in central Wisconsin almost required you to become a hunter. It didn't matter whether your passion was rabbits and squirrels, pheasants or ducks, deer or bear. Sometimes it was all of them and when everything was out of season, it was time to go ice fishing.

My father gave me my first firearm. I don't remember the model of the single shot .22 but the Leupold scope probably cost more than the rifle. "One shot, one kill" was the order of the day with headshots on small game required. During the winter we shot NRA targets indoors and in warmer weather we shot rats at the local garbage dump. You active shooters know how important technique and practice is.

Good optics are just as critical as the other components of successful shooting, especially when you have 20/400 vision. So the Leupold scope proved itself up to the task and resulted in a lot of game on the table. My father and I used to compete when we hunted and the tie breaker was often a partridge or quail shot out of the air when startled on your stalk.

This Bushnell Engage scope is perfect for my Ruger Precision .22. We live on 2.75 acres outside of town that is bordered by woods and wetlands. For some reason the snakes, bobcats and hawks can't keep the rat and rabbit populations under control -- which occasionally results in river rats in the attic and families of rabbits destroying my lawn and landscaping.

Being prey all of their lives has made these animals very difficult to surprise, so taking longer shots is critical to engagement. Having a good suppressor is important so that the neighbor's don't notice -- and it can also give you the opportunity for a second shot if necessary. (Fortunately that doesn't happen too often).

For the money, this is a very well built and engineered scope. The good field of view helps the shooter to discern the varmints through the thick plants, the glass is clear, the reticle does not overpower the target. and this scope balances well on my Ruger Precision Rimfire. My surging varmint population is now on a serious decline.
text_fidelity_b: Bushnell Engage Riflescope

text_fidelity_a: ZENY Adjustable Squat Rack Stand, Barbell Rack for Bench Press, Weight Lifting Rack for Home Gym Strength Training, Max Load 550LB These stands are great if you're on a budget or like me have have limited space. Very easy to assemble if you can look at a picture and read the list of what parts/bolts go where. It's not that hard on these stands, only a few bolts and the shorter ones are for the uprights. They're very sturdy once you get some weight on them. I used 45 lbs worth of dumbbells (2-25's and 2-20's) on the base and did a few bench presses and they didn't budge unracking or reracking. My first impression was these are going to be crap stands that are overpriced. I was wrong, they're really nice and the best part is that they can nest one on top of the other when not in use so you can save some space storing them. My only gripe would be that they have no rubber padding on the cradle or the safety catch. It's nothing I can't fix myself, just I think that's something that should come standard to not only protect your bar, but to reduce noise when reracking the bar. RAVE Sports Northern Lites Backcountry Snowshoe Speed Binding, Black, One Size Only the 2nd pair of snowshoes owned over the past +30 years. The old Sherpas are fine, but have been lusting over a pair of NorthernLites Backcountry for years. YOLO. Splurge. Outside of a significant weight savings, the binding system is nicer than the old Sherpas. Simple to put on or remove even with gloved hands. Only fiddling was tucking away the speed binding lace. Couple loops around the heel strap before tightening it.

Just in from the 4th hike. Logging an average of +9km per hike over rolling terrain in 6-12" of fresh light powder like snow. At 60kg these shoes are a bit on the too large size. Personal preference for 30"ers. The shoes track nice. Traction going up and down hill is good. Traversing a steeper face is a bit of an issue. No heel lift platform becomes an issue on longer, steeper climbs. Hit a short section of trail that was groomed for fat tire bikes. Real hard packed groomed. Shoe from some people trail runners left a minimal imprint. Left the snowshoes on for the couple hundred meters. Traction was excellent.

Expectations are for a durable product based on the past history of this brand of snowshoe.

Good for those looking for a light weight, easy on/off snowshoe for use in rolling terrain in fresh snow.

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Alta HR I came to this device from the Microsoft Band 2.0. So I was expecting a lack of functionality balanced by increased software support, community support and customization (bands).

This is a great minimal hardware design. Really like it. However software gates on cycling functionality (having to use your phone to start a “run” and convert it to a bike ride to see map data) are a bit annoying. If the user has turned on the connected GPS “feature,” why not just auto detect the bike ride AND show the map data when they're done?

The rotate wrist to turn on screen feature is accurate 50% of the time in real world usage. When you’re sitting at a desk or standing it is more like 90% accurate. When you are reclining on a couch, on your side, on your back, on your stomach, in bed, it does not work, at all. Get used to ensuring both arms are free so you can double tap the screen.

I purchased a braided metal band and the styling is great! I mean really nice compared to the Microsoft Band I owned previously. Almost elegant... I also like the professional look of the Alta HR with a black leather band.

After a week of use I would say that I probably should have purchased the Charge 2 HR or Charge 3 instead. They are also quite attractive, look good on a male wrist, and have significant additional functionality. Well I guess I"ll wait until the Charge 4 and hope it adds a GPS and returns to a chrome/brushed metal design similar to the Charge 2 HR (I’m not a fan of the finish options of the Charge 3).

Recommended for bikers as an inexpensive tracker if you tend to always have your phone on you and don’t mind activating ride tracking on your phone as a ”run” and converting it to a “ride” at the end of your session via phone app menus.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Alta HR

text_fidelity_a: MPOWERD Luci - The Original Inflatable Solar Light, Clear Finish I was laid off in Sept 2013 from a govt contract job. My family has been reduced to living in an RV. We are always looking for ways to reduce our expenses. I found this product by accident. I was at Big 5 buying a diamond knife sharpener. They had these sitting on the check out counter. The price was right at $12.99. I have used and made similar products in the past with mixed results, such as solar yard lights. I bought one. I turned it on when the sunset after charging for about an hour. We have our RV parked behind an abandoned house in the Arizona desert.  It gets real dark, real fast. This little light lit up our whole front yard area. It held the charge for a few hours. Inside the RV it was even better. I bought 3 more the next day! I have one in the bathroom, one in the living room, and two for the bedroom. I charge them by hanging then from our clothes line or one of the mesquite trees. I can get a few nights intermittent use from them on a single day in the sun. They have quickly become a necessary peice of gear for our involuntary reduced life style. When we spend a nice evening outside I place them in the trees and the four lights illuminate the yard better than 4 strands of 100 clear led xmas lights. I will buy more. We have friends in the homeless community and they will be getting these as gifts as funds allow. Waterproof, rugged, renewable. Two things would make them perfect, a USB port for emergency device charging,  and a photocell circut to allow them to charge during the day and come on automatically at night. I'm an Iraq war vet and I wish these were available in 2008. We were always losing power and we never lacked sunshine during the day. Batteries were not always available and being an avid reader due to insomnia, this product would have saved me many a boring night staring into darkness.
text_fidelity_b: MPOWERD Luci - The Original Inflatable Solar Light, Clear Finish

Lumintrail Center Mount Bicycle Kickstand - Bike Kick Stands for Adult Mountain, Cruiser and Road Bike - Quick Adjust Height Kickstand Fits Most 24, 26, 27.5, 29 Inches Bikes I installed this on a Cannondale Adventure 400 Hybrid with Jumbo frame. The installation was slightly difficult because the long installation bolt had trouble clearing my front derailleur bracket as I'd insert if from the top. This Cannondale bike has a built in cross-member with a hole for a kickstand and the bolt needs to go in from the top at an exact 90 degree angle. I finally managed to get it through w/o having to loosen the derailleur bracket. Once past that issue the installation was simple. You'll need large allen wrench to do it. It's not usually a wrench size found in a bike repair kit like an Alien wrench.

This kickstand operates and holds up my bike just fine. However, the adjustment button does stick out near my heel as I ride. I'm 6-4 and wear a size 15, so perhaps not an issue for smaller riders, but then smaller riders probably ride a smaller bike and have that kickstand set for a shorter length. I found I can loosen the attachment bolt and slightly reposition the kickstand to help keep this button closer to the lower chain-stay, but my foot can still catch it when my foot isn't completely straight on the pedal. Plus the adjustment made with the attachment bolt means the kickstand mount isn't as firmly locked in as I'd like given the shape of the mount.
text_fidelity_b: Lumintrail Center Mount Bicycle Kickstand - Bike Kick Stands for Adult Mountain, Cruiser and Road Bike - Quick Adjust Height Kickstand Fits Most 24, 26, 27.5, 29 Inches Bikes

Kryptonite New York Cinch Ring Security Chain (12mm x 75cm) withEVS4 Disc 14mm Shackle My experience with Kryptonite goes back to the period when one of their their original locks was found to be easily opened with a ballpoint pen. I had registered two of their motorcycle disc locks at that time and as soon as they changed the design they sent me two new replacement locks. Since then I have become older and moved from motorcycles to bicycles.

I previously submitted a review of the very excellent Saris Bike Porter 2-Bike Trunk Rack, which has design features that enable bikes to be securely locked to the rack and also allow the rack to be locked to the frame of my car, under the rear bumper. Kryptonite's 2.25' New York Noose is just the right length to lock the top tubes of two bikes to the beefy upper section of the Saris rack with their Evolution Series 4 Disc Lock, and their KryptoFlex 3/8" x 7' Double Loop Security Cable is perfect to go through the front wheels of both bikes and lock the bottom frame of the rack to the frame of my car with one of the replacement locks they sent me many years ago, which is similar to their current KryptoLok Series 2 Disc Lock. Both of these Kryptonite locks, and the chain and cable, work perfectly and I have never encountered any problems with them.

We don't need this level of security for most of our bicycle outings, but when we head out for a vacation with our bikes that includes stays at multiple motels we always use our Kryptonite locks and chains.

text_fidelity_a:
Ultralight Portable Outdoor Backpacking Canister Camp Stove with Piezo Ignition 3.9oz (Silvery Stove and Orange Box) Great little stove, love the piezo lighter. Fits inside a hiking pot with a fuel canister, very easy to keep with you and very fast to set up. Perfect for a hot cup of coffee or some soup while out in the woods or while taking a break from work. For the cost of a couple foofy coffee drinks from Starbucks, you can have fresh coffee wherever. This much utility for this cost can't be beat.

For those unfamiliar with micro canister stoves, there are some limitations. This is definitely is a backpacking stove, and nothing like a Coleman suitcase or even one of the older green single burner Colemans. This stove is optimized for light weight and compromises have been made in support of that goal. The pot supports are small and somewhat wobbly and the base is your canister, so smaller canisters are less stable. Definitely not meant for large pots, even a full 1liter pot is pretty wobbly. I've had trouble making enough coffee for 3 people with each of us wanting to fill our 20+ oz insulated travel mugs, even though the stove cranks out plenty enough BTUs. Wound up stacking up bricks around the stove to support the pot independent of the stove, so all the stove had to do was pump out BTU's. This is not a detraction, just something to be aware of, as heating 2+ liters of water for a group is NOT what this stove is designed for.

I use this for a quick cup of coffee or some hot soup while camping/shooting/wrenching/whatever. Morale booster, mostly. I've had no issues with reliability, but if I was in any kind of situation where the stove failing would be more than an inconvenience, I'd cough up for the peace of mind of an MSR. Sure it's 4-5 times the cost, but that's only $30.

Note: There are adapters all over the web to use these with the very inexpensive tall skinny butane cans, or even to refill the isobutane canisters with just butane. For the average hiker using a stove a few times per year, not enough fuel will be used for fuel cost to matter. If you're using it more frequently, one of those adapters could pay for itself quickly. Straight butane won't work as well as isobutane in cooler weather, but if you're getting into temps that low you should probably look at a liquid fueled stove anyway.

Wow that got long.
text_fidelity_b: Ultralight Portable Outdoor Backpacking Canister Camp Stove with Piezo Ignition 3.9oz (Silvery Stove and Orange Box)

text_fidelity_a:
Large 35L Hiking Backpack - Packable Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack Water Resistant Cycling Hicking Small Outdoor Backpack Women Men I admit I am slow to write reviews. I want to see how a product holds up in the long haul.

This HEXIN 35L pack has held up and performed wonderfully!!!

Initially I purchased this to take with me to Ireland because I wanted to do a lot of exploring without dragging around large amounts of bags to encompass my gear. It was still in its comfy EASY TO USE self-pouch when I got to the Emerald Isle.

The first day I really used it was a lovely rainy Irish morning. I put all my gear in, from sensitive electronics to water bottles in the side pouches (hugely helpful to not have to dig in bag for a drink). Stored my inn keys and passport in the inner pocket where they were safe but not easily removed from my pack without notice.

I carried my larger Pixelbook, cameras and assortments; Change of clothes and extra layers to add or shed as needed; snacks and even an extra pair of hike boots in the bottom in case I didn't want to tromp around in wet boots.

There are so many pockets and secure dividers. This pack is well made. I have (before and since) tried a variety of styles and brands and I only swear by Hexin. It has lasted two full years and is still water resistant (and been through a LOT of rain), the zippers are still strong and safely covered. I can be really rough on gear, but I clean it after each adventure and I have had NO issues.

There is also a bright orange whistle which, I have only used for my dog, but is great for a small woman to have in emergency.

I love that I can also stick stuff in the straps in the mesh pockets and under the elastic band. You never know.

The straps and pack are nicely designed so they are always comfortable no matter what I stuff in the bag,

I love that when I am not using it I can fold it down so small that it lays flat in the bottom of my bag.

I am back to purchase another HEXIN now because I have given up on the rest. This is a really great bag. At 35L it holds more than enough gear, clothes, etc., and keeps things protected. I highly recommend it and that does not come lightly.

Bottom line: BEST BAG EVER!!!
text_fidelity_b: Large 35L Hiking Backpack - Packable Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack Water Resistant Cycling Hicking Small Outdoor Backpack Women Men

text_fidelity_a:
Valor Fitness BD-7 Power Rack - Squat Rack and Bench Press Power Cage with LAT Pulldown Attachment and Other Workout Rack Bundle Options for a Complete Weightlifting Home Gym I bought this 2 months ago to the day. I wanted to write a review, but I wanted to give it time for the excitement to wear off so I could give a more everyday impression of it.

My quick background as a lifter... I'm in my early 30s, been lifting since my mid 20s... only recently got my diet and routine dialed in though. Anyway, I always knew I wanted a home gym, as whether I go to a local gym near work or home I lose a good 30-40 minutes getting there and coming back. My wife likes working out but hates the gym environment as well.

Alright, enough of my life story... how is the RACK?

Assembly was pretty easy. Just get a hand drill with a 3/8" socket adapter, a 17mm socket and a 17mm wrench. I think that's all I needed. Instructions were pretty straightforward and it took about an hour. The cage itself feels pretty high quality... I can see myself using this for decades.

Using the rack itself is pretty good. I have it in a room that is 11x12' in size, with a vertical leg press machine, a plate tree and some plastic dressers. The room is definitely full, but I can move around and have enough room to either go through my routines, which are all supersets, or to be in the room with my wife while she works out without feeling like we are on top of each other.

I know what you want to know. WHAT IS THE DEAL WITH THE PULLEYS? Well I have used them 4-5x per week for the last 2 months, and so far they feel great. I tried various things to lubricate the pulley shaft... the last thing I tried was Vaseline, but I haven't touched that in weeks. Ultimately it works, though I do wish it had more sophisticated bearings for the weight holder itself. I read some reviews about the pulleys getting chewed up so I pre-emptively ordered some metal pulleys... I have not installed them yet though. The stock units are working fine so far, even when I load them up with ~170+ lbs. The unit just feels very solid.

My only gripe, and it's so minor I don't feel it's enough to take any stars off, is when I rack bench weight in the cage the unit leans back a little bit. It needs stabilizing feet in front and in the back. But that is really minor. It doesn't feel like the unit is going to fall backwards or is dangerous at all. Other thing is the weight holders are too close together. I would love more space to have the flexibility to put 45s on both levels.

So to sum up here are the pros and cons from my POV:

Pros:
- Phenomenal price
- Good build quality
- High/low pulleys work great even with heavy weight
- Quick and easy assembly
- Height gives enough clearance for chinups

Cons (really minor):
- Unit tips back a little bit when racking barbell for bench
- Weight holders are too close together for Olympic 45s on both levels

I am a bit neurotic when it comes to a lot of things, and I am an engineer, so I am more relieved than anything that this works so well. It's a simple but effective design and an incredible value. If you can wean yourself off of fancy machines and stick with free weights this should cover all your needs and render HELLA GAINS.
text_fidelity_b: Valor Fitness BD-7 Power Rack - Squat Rack and Bench Press Power Cage with LAT Pulldown Attachment and Other Workout Rack Bundle Options for a Complete Weightlifting Home Gym

text_fidelity_a:
TETON Sports TrailHead Sleeping Bag; Lightweight Camping, Hiking , Scout Green, 75" x 30" x 20" We ordered these bags for overnight/weekend backpacking trips. We aren't ultralight backpackers, since we stick to 1-2 nights, but this bag was still lighter than most we considered, so I was grateful for that. We have other Teton products that we use with car camping, so we are familiar with the company and their customer service and products.

First, the bags are fairly light at just 2lb 9 oz. Great for weekend backpackers. They also compress nicely in the sack they came with, but would do so even more if you bought a compression bag. However, they easily fit in the bottom sleeping bag compartment of our backpacks as is. The sack also has a strap on one end so you can easily attach it to the outside of your pack.

The bag is warm, and it's important to remember that sleeping bag ratings are for SURVIVAL and assume you're properly dressed for the weather you're using the bag in--dry base layer or naked, hat, etc. This bag should keep you comfortable at 40F and above if you're properly dressed/dry. If you go to bed in the same clothes you've been wearing all day, you'll get cold in any sleeping bag--always put on clean, dry clothes or sleep naked with a hat. :) If you're worried about warmth, you can easily add a lightweight fleece mummy bag liner--it won't add much weight to your pack, and the extra warmth can be reassuring if you need it.

I'm recovering from thyroid cancer and have gained 80lbs, so even as a plus size women at 5'10, 250 lbs, I have plenty of room to zip up and around me so that the bag isn't cold. I'm a side sleeper and I move around a lot at night, but I don't try to roll IN the bag--I roll with the bag. The cinch hood is a nice feature for a bag at this price.

Overall, yes, there are lighter and warmer backpacking bags--but for this price point, you'd be hard pressed to find one as warm, light, and soft as this one. If you're a beginner or just do 1-2 night trips from spring, summer, early fall, this bag should exceed your expectations. Add a lightweight fleece liner and you'll be set for even cooler temps. Teton never disappoints.
text_fidelity_b: TETON Sports TrailHead Sleeping Bag; Lightweight Camping, Hiking , Scout Green, 75" x 30" x 20"

text_fidelity_a:
Moxi Skates - Beach Bunny - Fashionable Womens Roller Skates Color: Watermelon. Skate Size: 7 (My normal shoe/boot size is 8-8.5 in US womens)
First, they are soooo cute! I love the color combo. I'm 50 yrs old and decided to get back into roller skating. I used to do this casually when I was in my teens, but was never exceptional at it. I thought this would be a fun way to get some more exercise in my life. So far its working! You engage so many muscles when roller skating. It takes balance, core and leg strength to keep from falling on your bum. These are made of vinyl so they are quite stiff at first and take some time break in. My hubby purchased these as a gift. He purchased according to the size chart and they fit well/snug with a thick sock. I normally wear a size 8 in U.S women’s shoes. When it comes to boots I typically buy 8.5 (to allow for thicker sock). Hubby purchased the size 7 skates as the chart indicated. This was just right. I thought they might be a bit tight at first. But with use, I realized the size was perfect. You want your foot to be held firmly as you will be moving around a lot. I imagine if they were looser, my foot would flex more and potentially cause strain in the foot muscles so I think the snug sizing is perfect. Measure your foot and look at size chart and you should be fine. I like that the skates have a metal base plate instead of plastic. This feels sturdier/safer. The wheels roll well on blacktop streets (even better on my hardwood floors inside my house). There are a couple things that were a bit odd. First the vinyl is so thick its a bit uncomfortable (specifically around the ankle) until they get worn in. And it takes a while to wear them in.
Second, the laces on one skate were a whole foot longer than the laces on the other skate. This trips out my OCD brain. I will have to replace them.

Overall, I think these are good skates for beginners (of all ages). They are made well and of good quality. Just be patient with the wear in period.
text_fidelity_b: Moxi Skates - Beach Bunny - Fashionable Womens Roller Skates

text_fidelity_a: HOTaitai Portable Butane Stove with Wind Guard and Carrying Case, Single Burner Gas Stove Sutiable for Camping Emergency Preparedness I got this (and a propane heater) for emergency blackout times.  The blizzard this year in Texas in February saw me in a house for five days with no heat, no electricity while keeping my kitchen and bathroom faucets on a running trickle so they didn't freeze.  I made it through those five days because I wore three layers of clothing, two pairs of socks, two hats and covered up with three blankets, plus I had water to drink, bread and peanut butter to eat...yep, I learned my lesson.  This burner will be an emergency way to heat water or food should the power ever go out like that again.  I have had this burner on outside and it works great.  Bought a 6-pack of the 1 pound propane canisters and just in case, I have a back up to this back up with the smaller, hiker's version that runs on the small sterno cans which I also got in a 6-pack.  The point is that this can be used in your yard as a side-by-side to your BBQ grill to heat up the chili to smother your grilled hot dog in or if you are sitting in your house, in the dark and need something hot in your belly - tea or tomato soup - this little burner can do the job.  I understand that you do have to be careful of the fumes, but I also have a carbon monoxide detector that I watch when using this item in the house.  This stove top is so easy to use - insert the propane canister, turn the knob to start and then adjust the flame to what you need and then turn it off when done.  When cool, remove the propane, put it back in the case and you're ready for it's next use.  Pricewise, I think it's fairly reasonable for summer camping and emergency use.
text_fidelity_b: HOTaitai Portable Butane Stove with Wind Guard and Carrying Case, Single Burner Gas Stove Sutiable for Camping Emergency Preparedness

text_fidelity_a: Gaiam Pilates Total Toning Kit When looking for 2 lb weights I opted for these rather than more traditional weights because a) they looked like it would be possible to extend all the fingers while holding the weights if you want more length in the arm.  and b) They seemed to have the weight distributed evenly on both the palm side and the back side of the hand.  Previously, I thought weighted gloves were the answer, but they all have their weight on the back of the hand only, which exercises different muscles than if you were to have the weight mostly in the palm.  After trying out these weights I must say that I'm very happy.  These not only have even weight distribution on both sides of each hand, but you also have the option of letting go your grip and extending your fingers out fully while doing many exercises without worrying about the weights dropping.  The DVD has 3 15 minute workouts which are great for either a warm-up into a more lengthy workout, or for something quick in the morning to wake me up and get me going.  The only issue I have is the videography of the dvd.  The camera person apparently felt there was a need to switch camera angles every 5 seconds.  Very distracting. It wouldn't have bothered me as much if I was able to see the whole body of the instructor more often, but I've done the standing workout is the one I've done the most and often the video shoots the top half of her body without showing what she's doing with her legs... and switches to show her feet and not showing what she's doing with her arms!  I'm sure after I do it several more times I'll be able to just do the upper & lower half movements without needing to see her do them, but when you're first learning a movement is when it's most important to continually see it so that you're sure you get it right.  Especially if you're like me and don't get choreography down very quickly.  It would've been better if they just stuck to one or two camera angles and stayed there rather than switching constantly.
text_fidelity_b: Gaiam Pilates Total Toning Kit

text_fidelity_a:
EUROBIKE G7 Folding Mountain Bike,27.5 Inch Full Suspension Mountain Bike for Men,21 Speeds Mens and Womens Mountain Bicycle,Dual Disc Brake Adult Foldable Bike I could be four stars...
I was looking for a foldable bike to put in a car trunk. Other similar bikes, just half the price, are all shipped from china with 2-3 month wait time with no reviews or 2-3 reviews with 5 stars. Granted they all are made in the same shop from the same chinesium but this one has 30+ positive and was delivered in 4 days.
The good. Frame is steal and well welded and painted. Its heavy but sturdy. Front fork is just as good but has a little play in the springs, not critical. Rear suspension is good enough. Rims are straight.
The so-so. I am 5-11 and set the seat is almost as high as it gets. The handle bar could be higher at my preference.
The bad. Worst thing - the brake disks mounting. Front wheel all six and four on the rear wheel had broken threads. This is a major screwup as the wheels are all aluminum and the only way to fix it is to thread next size 6mm threads. Techicaly, easy fix but this should never happen! Next - the shifters are the cheapest i have seen. The left 3-grear broke while adjusting it. The push lever was grinding the base that caused the latch pin to deflect. I expected to replace them anyhow so it wasnt a show stopper.
And the special thing - the hand pump. This bike comes with a hand pump. I dont know what happened to it, either a $1-per hour laborer or rats on the container ship, either one is a shame for a bike with this price tag, but the pump was all chewed up. Dont believe me - see the pictures
So, two things, the disk brake screws and shifter - two stars,
I would not recommend this bike but there are not too many alternatives. Well, unless you are willing to take the risk and order one from china with no reviews.
text_fidelity_b: EUROBIKE G7 Folding Mountain Bike,27.5 Inch Full Suspension Mountain Bike for Men,21 Speeds Mens and Womens Mountain Bicycle,Dual Disc Brake Adult Foldable Bike

text_fidelity_a:
SOG Throwing Knives with Sheath 3 Pack Balanced Throwing Knives Set w/ Paracord Knife Handles and Professional Throwing Knife Sheath (F041TN-CP) I'm a knife/hatchet/weapon collector with probably over 400 blades in my collection. My first strong impression is always from seeing the blade, some just jump out at me from a visually striking perspective. In my experience, if they look good in a picture, they'll feel good in my hand. Very few times have I been disappointed in a blade purchase--if so, I just give it away--but I've learned to trust my instincts. I'm not talking about the weird fantasy stuff you see out there, I collect practicable and usable blades both old and new, some inexpensive but a good value, and some unbelievably expensive and worth it only for the investment value.

First off, I own three SOG products: a large Creed knife, an SOG Access Card, and a Tactical Tomahawk. All represent good value for the money and are well-constructed for their purpose. So it was a no-brainer for me to order the SOG Throwing Knives. But wait, these are more than throwing knives. Let me point out a few positives:

1. They are well designed, made of relatively thick steel, have a long cutting edge, and are well balanced.
2. The long cutting edge makes them much more than only a thrower, the grip is comfortable and the choils help prevent your hand from slipping forward to the blade.
3. They can be comfortably and effectively handled with stabbing, slashing, and back handed grips.
4. They will obviously handle any cutting chores assigned to them--once you sharpen the blades properly.
5. If not used to make tent pegs, they are long enough to be used as tent pegs in a pinch.
6. The paracord on the handles could be unwrapped and used for a multiple of purposes in the field.

And of course there are some negatives, but they aren't deal breakers considering the price:

1. Mine did not come sharp. That is easily rectified with a proper sharpening and can quickly be brought to the desired edge.
2. The sheath, while of a practical design, is not strongly made and I would expect it to not hold up long under constant use.
3. Although well balanced, I prefer throwing knives that are double edged at the tip and that are also longer and with more weight. At my size these feel insubstantial.

But I have to say, for this pricing point, this is a nice package to consider including in your bug out bag. You can wear them on your belt, they don't weigh much, and you get three strong blades for the price of one. Just make sure that you also have an excellent folding knife, a sharp and durable fixed blade knife, and a strong tactical tomahawk in your kit. It's always better to have too much of something than nothing at all. And by the way, almost anyone with moderate coordination can learn to throw a knife effectively. Just check out the You-Tube videos and try it out. Lots of fun!
text_fidelity_b: SOG Throwing Knives with Sheath 3 Pack Balanced Throwing Knives Set w/ Paracord Knife Handles and Professional Throwing Knife Sheath (F041TN-CP)

GLUREE 4 Stands Braided Fishing Line with Line Outlet Box 328Yards/300m 15-50LB PE Multifilament Braided Wire Smoother Mainline Level Low Memory Good Watercutting I have never used braided line before so I thought I'd give it a try. It promises to reduce professional overlap....and that would be marvelous. At the time of writing it will be bit before I get to put it to the fish test. I ordered 15# multicolored line. I'll say this much...it comes in a NICE plastic box with a doodad that lets you unspool to your reel right from inside that same box. Most impressive. If I'm this delighted by the superior packaging I can't wait to get it on the water. If the thought put into the product matches the end result then wow! I'll be back a little later with the report.

Part Deux: Finally had a chance to go test out my new GLUREE 4 Stands Braided Fishing Line in a local public lake a few minutes ago. I wrapped it around a new reel, so you might call it a multi-test. I tied on a pretty hefty crankbait, and first cast and several more I got that nasty pverlap. I kept fiddling with the reel until I pretty much eliminated that mess. In the meantime I found that correcting the line was easier than I ever had in the past.

Part Tre: I guess I'm the only guy who didn't know that braided line doesn't break. Subsequently I have been enlightened by no less than two different fishing pals. When you go braided, which I like a lot, you really need to tie on a leader with regular monofilament fishing line attached at the end so when you get hung up you can break off when you put on the old tug. Braided is strong stuff!

The line itself, even at 15#, is like handling sewing thread. As it spools out of the handy box you get different colors. (I'd love to know the yardage per different color.) In the water the line is easy to see while working the lure. I doubt the fish would mind. So, if you haven't tried braided line before, you should go for it. I'll be putting it to the big test a little later in the season. As of this writing, still a little early. So far I like it better than the plastic stuff.
text_fidelity_b: GLUREE 4 Stands Braided Fishing Line with Line Outlet Box 328Yards/300m 15-50LB PE Multifilament Braided Wire Smoother Mainline Level Low Memory Good Watercutting

Auoxer Fitness Exercise Weighted Hoola Hoop, Detachable and Size Adjustable Design, Lose Weight Fast by Fun Way, Fat Burning Healthy Model Sports Life This Auoxer hula hoop comes with no instructions or suggestions. The picture on the box is the only hint as to its assembly however, it is fairly intuitive. The difficulty is joining segments 5 and 6 if you want the smallest opening size. It requires some muscle to force the ends to line up. I sat in bed and pushed the opposite (assembled) end against the top of my foot to force it into a somewhat round shape so I could join 5 to 6. The more segments used the easier it is to assemble.

Disassembly is more difficult and don't do it after a fresh manicure - it can be a nail breaker. You have to roll back about an inch of the foam covering and find the orange button, depress it hard, then continue depressing as you pull the segments apart. This alone will burn a few calories. Personally, I'll only be using it at home so I won't be disassembling it.

The opening size by number of segments:
6 segment opening size: 26”
7 segment opening size: 31”
8 segment opening size: 35”

There is a mild chemical-like plastic smell, but after 2 days out in the garage it went away.

I suppose if the assembly/disassembly were easier the hula hoop might not hold up to repeated use, so I forgive that difficulty. I do like that it's adjustable and the foam covering is a nice touch. Now if only I could remember how I hula hooped as a kid. I used to have simultaneous hoops on both arms and my waist while moving around. Now I have to concentrate to keep this one hoop from falling to the ground! That's ok, it will come back to me and in the meantime I have some hearty laughs each morning.

The red or green dot has several brightness settings by clicking the button each time for higher or to lower the brightness. A simple press of both buttons will turn off the red or green light leaving it in the same brightness position for the next time you use it. You can also just press and hold the red or green button for 2 seconds and the light will go off. Both the red and green dots are precision with clear circle views. The front honeycomb lens cover can be removed with a special tool but I like it for focusing the dot faster and it acts as a sun shade.

Overall construction looks good. It weighs 11.4 ounces. The flip up covers lock tight in a closed position, but you will need to reposition them to the side of the scope so not to interfere with the sights while open or you can simply remove them when using the scope. The fiber optic site works good with little outside light and during the evening hours but not where it is pitch black. The accessories in the description were supposed to be 3 Allen wrenches but this sight came with one for removing the scope from the mount. If you have a good set of Allen wrenches handy, this is not a problem. My testing was on an AR short barrel. This scope should work good on most air soft too.

This is certainly a good value for an ACOG style scope in my opinion. The buttons and sight settings are all in fingers reach. I have other Pinty products that are dependable and have lasted a long time.

text_fidelity_a: Adventure Medical Kits Heatsheets Survival Blanket For Two Person, (Pack of 2) For many years, I carried around those Mylar 'space blankets' whenever I went camping, kept them in my car, packed them in my emergency kits, and used them under my clothes to keep toasty warm in the winter.  They were inexpensive, lightweight, but always felt a little small and too flimsy for more than two or three uses.  As such, I always wished someone made nicer heat-reflecting blankets, still at an affordable price - and Adventure Medical Kits delivers.  Each blanket is large enough to make a decent shelter, beef up a tent or makeshift shelter, or for two people to wrap themselves in.  They aren't as crinkly or loud as the older space blankets, which is also nice.  They come packed in very compact, taking up only a little more room and weight than the older smaller space blankets.  They unfold easily, with various instructions printed right on the blanket.  While it seems impossible to fold it up as compact as they come from the factory, they do still fold up pretty nice (I roll it up, and then flatten it out).  I have one blanket I've used dozens of times, and it's only just starting to show some wear here and there.  For the price, I definitely got my money's worth, many times over.  I recommend everyone have one or more in their car or home, in case of emergency.  For anyone involved in outdoor sports, these are phenomenal.  It's another great product from Adventure Medical Kits!
text_fidelity_b: Adventure Medical Kits Heatsheets Survival Blanket For Two Person, (Pack of 2)

text_fidelity_a:
Moultrie Digital Picture Viewer, Black, 2 x 6 x 8.25 I like the viewer pretty well overall. I will tell you what I like first. It's fairly compact. The rubber grip surfaces make it easier to hold. I like that it has uses 4 AAA batteries. Devices with 4 batteries USUALLY have very long battery life, in my experience. It appears that all the covers to the buttons and hatches, etc, are water resistant and maybe waterproof. I like the positive slide on-off "click" of the power button. I love that I can leave one 16gb flashcard internal, and plug in a 2nd flashcard, and then without looking at any of the pictures, transfer everything off the 2nd card to the 1st card (assuming there's room), and then put the 2nd card back into the trail camera. That might be this viewer's best feature--the 2 SD card slots feature. The screen is adequate, altho I feel to really look at the pics, you should look at them on a laptop or desktop computer.

OK, here's what I don't like. I don't like the SD card sticking out of the bottom of the viewer. I would rather it be pressed into the slot and catch with the spring-loaded catch like the internal card slot, and be able to completely close the cover on the SD card. BUT, I realize they may have made it that way so you could take the card out with gloves on, cold fingers, etc. I also don't like how that rubber flap kinda hangs in the breeze when I peel it off to insert a card. I don't like how you can't see all the pics on the screen in a matrix (unless I haven't figured that out yet, and if I'm wrong, I will apologize) and choose from them. I don't like how you have to scroll thru the pics. I also think it takes too long to transfer photos from the trail cam card to the internal card.

I know I'm being nit-picky about some of my dislikes, but I still gave it 4 stars. Oh, also, I paid about $65 (with shipping) not on Amazon Prime, because it wasn't available for Prime when I ordered it, and I noticed today that it was about $51 on Amazon Prime from another vendor. Oh well, it's a decent buy, for sure at $51 and Prime shipping, and an OK buy at $65.
text_fidelity_b: Moultrie Digital Picture Viewer, Black, 2 x 6 x 8.25

text_fidelity_a: Portable Heated Seat Cushion, 3 Mode Adjustable Thin Heat Heating Cushion, 【No Power Bank】USB Power Heated Foldable Back Chair Pad, Memory Foam Heated Seat Pad for Indoor, Outdoor, Sports, Beach Winter is so much easier to bear when your behind is warm, right?  I had tried another one meant for the car, also with a USB cord and while it warmed, the part against my back began to dig into my back and hurt.  I mean, it may have been a bit more padded than this one, but it had no "give" so that I didn't feel IT under me, if that makes sense. My low rating is mainly because these are missing the most important tip type for mountain hiking. I also rated TheFitLife and Cascade Mountain Tech poles low because of their short life span.
